t: Find Common Elements Between Two Arrays
o: answer1 counts positions in nums1 whose value appears anywhere in nums2, and vice versa. Membership, not multiplicity, matters. Convert each array to a set and count elements present in the other set — or brute-force with nested loops given sizes <= 100.
k: Convert to sets for O(1) membership tests.
Duplicates count once per occurrence in the original array, so count over the array, not the set.
Symmetric structure: the same membership test applied in both directions.

a.i: For each element of nums1 scan nums2, and vice versa. Trivially correct for n,m <= 100.
s: For each x in nums1, check whether any y in nums2 equals x; tally.
Do the symmetric pass for nums2.
a.t: O(n*m) — each element scanned against the other array.

a.i: Build a set from each array, then count array elements contained in the opposite set in linear time.
s: Count nums1 elements in set2 and nums2 elements in set1.
a.t: O(n + m) — set construction plus linear scans.

w: Trivial problem; the interview point is recognizing duplicates are counted per-index (example 2: nums1 = [4,3,2,3,1] gives 3, not 2). Values bounded by 100 also allow boolean arrays instead of hash sets. Follow-up: return the distinct common values, or handle streaming inputs.
